item.title: SoMoBench: a quasi-global benchmark dataset for data-driven soil moisture modelling with in situ-derived targets
item.description:
SoMoBench: a quasi-global benchmark dataset for data-driven soil moisture modelling with in situ-derived targets
Sungmin O, Rene Orth, and Wouter Dorigo
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-620,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Machine learning is increasingly used for soil moisture modelling, but models remain difficult to compare because studies use different data and tests. Here, we present SoMoBench, built from ground measurements at 1,445 locations across diverse climate conditions, covering 2001–2024 and three soil depths. It also provides weather data, site information, baseline model results, and example code. This resource supports more consistent model development and fairer comparisons.

item.title: A Global Soil Dataset for Earth System Modeling (Version 2, GSDEv2)
item.description:
A Global Soil Dataset for Earth System Modeling (Version 2, GSDEv2)
Gaosong Shi, Anne Gobin, Zhongwang Wei, Hua Yuan, Qingliang Li, Wei Shangguan, and Yongjiu Dai
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-770,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
We developed a new global soil dataset that maps 20 important soil properties across six depth ranges at high spatial detail. It combines soil observations from around the world with environmental information and regional soil products. Tests showed improved average prediction accuracy, while land-surface experiments demonstrated the importance of soil data for simulations.

item.title: SgriWind-CN: A Sub-Daily Gridded High-Resolution Near-Surface Wind Speed Dataset for China, Generated by an AI-Driven Integration of In-Situ Observations
item.description:
SgriWind-CN: A Sub-Daily Gridded High-Resolution Near-Surface Wind Speed Dataset for China, Generated by an AI-Driven Integration of In-Situ Observations
Xueru Bai, Mingyuan Zhang, Jinlin Zha, Anning Huang, Xinsheng Zhu, Jian Tang, Deming Zhao, and Jian Wu
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-806,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Reliable near-surface wind speed data underpin a wide range of research in hydrology, climatology, wind energy, and environmental change. Here, we release the SgriWind-CN dataset, a sub-daily, gridded wind-speed dataset over China, generated from 6-hourly observations at 2,384 meteorological stations. This study aims to provide a robust, high-resolution data foundation for understanding wind variability and its broader impacts across Earth system sciences.
